parts:
Hello group,

I searched the previous posts and couldn't find anything on this.
I ran the same models in Presence and Unmarked.
The models have the same AIC and comparable parameter estimates for PSI
but the SEs for unmarked are consistently  larger in unmarked (see example below)

I would greatly appreciate any thoughts on the matter

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] paramater estimates have different STD. Error in unmarked and presence
parts:
Thanks!  There are two issues:  (1) VegHt needs to be scaled (either dividing by 10 or standardizing) for PRESENCE to pretty much match the output from occu and (2) PRESENCE doesn't warn you of the problem.  (But I used probably an old version of PRESENCE (6.4) which might account for that.)  (It's probably always a good idea to either standardize predictor variables or run it both ways (standardized and unstandardized) as a quality assurance check.  And I'd say that goes especially for mixed models.)
 
If you divide VegHt by 10, then one obtains the following results:
 
PRESENCE

Untransformed Estimates of coefficients for covariates (Beta's)
======================================================================
                         estimate   std.error

A1   psi             :  -3.874362    1.986970
A2   psi.VegHt       :   0.493140    0.339655
B1   p1              :   0.630795    0.301144
 
 
occu
 
Occupancy:
Estimate      SE        z     P(>|z|)

(Intercept)   -3.867       2.002    -1.93  0.0534
VegHt          0.492       0.342     1.44  0.1507
 
Detection:
Estimate     SE      z    P(>|z|)

0.631     0.301   2.1  0.0361
 
I've attached the PRESENCE test.pao file and the R code is given below:
 
# Load unmarked
  library(unmarked)

# Get data
  d = read.csv("unmarkedTestData.csv")
   
# Format data for occupancy analysis in unmarked
  dUMF <- with(d, {
    unmarkedFrameOccu(
    y = cbind(n1, n2, n3, n4, n5, n6, n7),
    siteCovs = data.frame(VegHt=VegHt/10))
  })
# Get parameter estimates
  occu(~1 ~VegHt, data=dUMF)
 
 
Jim

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] paramater estimates have different STD. Error in unmarked and presence
parts:
Just as a follow-up, I wondered what might the estimates be if calculations were done with a bit more precision (as I assume that both PRESENCE and unmarked use double-precision numbers).  I did a brute-force program in Mathematica using 100 significant digits and found the following (but displaying only the first 20 significant digits):

Parameter   Estimate                 Std. Err.
Intercept   -3.8743623940735438113   2.0034612223160102579
VegHt       0.049314037954389727888  0.034247365356409299073
logit(p)    0.63079516665049360084   0.30114368077641836659

With more precision one doesn't have to standardize the predictor variables as often.  (But, of course, code will take longer to execute.)

The Mathematica code is given below:

(* VegHt for sites with no detections *)
vegHt0 = Rationalize[{42.57, 40.2, 40.39, 70.82, 74.78, 45.87, 44.16, 
    47.29, 73.01, 61.77,
    45.87, 38.56, 37.29, 65.28, 36.32, 44.45, 46.39, 52.83, 55.63, 
    54.76, 54.91, 58.98}];
(* VegHt for sites with at least one detection *)
vegHt1 = Rationalize[{60.05, 85.95, 55.52, 50.7, 42.32, 49.12, 74.78}];
(* Total number of detections for sites with with at least one detection *)
m = {4, 3, 6, 5, 7, 2, 5};

(* Number of sites with no detectins *)
 n0 = Length[vegHt0];
(* Number of sites with at least one detection *)
n1 = Length[vegHt1];
(* Visits per site *)
v = 7;

(* Create log likelihood function *)
psi0 = 1 - 1/(1 + Exp[a + b vegHt0]);
psi1 = 1 - 1/(1 + Exp[a + b vegHt1]);
p = 1 - 1/(1 + Exp[logitp]);
loglikelihood = 
  Sum[Log[1 - psi0[[i]] + psi0[[i]] (1 - p)^v], {i, n0}] +
   Sum[Log[psi1[[i]]], {i, n1}] + 
   Total[m] Log[p] + (v*n1 - Total[m]) Log[1 - p];

(* Find maximum likelihood estimates of a, b, and p *)
sol = NMinimize[{-2 loglikelihood + 2*3}, {a, b, logitp}, 
   WorkingPrecision -> 100, MaxIterations -> 50];
N[sol, 20]

(* Estimated variance/covariance matrix *)
plogL = D[loglikelihood, {{a, b, logitp}}];
plogL2 = D[plogL, {{a, b, logitp}}];
var = -Inverse[plogL2 /. sol[[2]]];

(* Standard errors of parameter estimates *)
sea = N[var[[1, 1]]^(1/2), 20]
seb = N[var[[2, 2]]^(1/2), 20]
sep = N[var[[3, 3]]^(1/2), 20]

parts:
Dear Jim,

interesting stuff, thanks, but something seems to be off by a factor 10 in the coefficient of vegHt.

Best regards  ---  Marc

From: unma...@googlegroups.com [unma...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of Jim Baldwin [jbald...@gmail.com]
Sent: 02 January 2016 02:54
To: unma...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [unmarked] paramater estimates have different STD. Error in unmarked and presence

Just as a follow-up, I wondered what might the estimates be if calculations were done with a bit more precision (as I assume that both PRESENCE and unmarked use double-precision numbers).  I did a brute-force program in Mathematica using 100 significant digits and found the following (but displaying only the first 20 significant digits):

Parameter   Estimate                 Std. Err.
Intercept   -3.8743623940735438113   2.0034612223160102579
VegHt       0.049314037954389727888  0.034247365356409299073
logit(p)    0.63079516665049360084   0.30114368077641836659

With more precision one doesn't have to standardize the predictor variables as often.  (But, of course, code will take longer to execute.)

The Mathematica code is given below:

(* VegHt for sites with no detections *)
vegHt0 = Rationalize[{42.57, 40.2, 40.39, 70.82, 74.78, 45.87, 44.16, 
    47.29, 73.01, 61.77,
    45.87, 38.56, 37.29, 65.28, 36.32, 44.45, 46.39, 52.83, 55.63, 
    54.76, 54.91, 58.98}];
(* VegHt for sites with at least one detection *)
vegHt1 = Rationalize[{60.05, 85.95, 55.52, 50.7, 42.32, 49.12, 74.78}];
(* Total number of detections for sites with with at least one detection *)
m = {4, 3, 6, 5, 7, 2, 5};

(* Number of sites with no detectins *)
 n0 = Length[vegHt0];
(* Number of sites with at least one detection *)
n1 = Length[vegHt1];
(* Visits per site *)
v = 7;

(* Create log likelihood function *)
psi0 = 1 - 1/(1 + Exp[a + b vegHt0]);
psi1 = 1 - 1/(1 + Exp[a + b vegHt1]);
p = 1 - 1/(1 + Exp[logitp]);
loglikelihood = 
  Sum[Log[1 - psi0[[i]] + psi0[[i]] (1 - p)^v], {i, n0}] +
   Sum[Log[psi1[[i]]], {i, n1}] + 
   Total[m] Log[p] + (v*n1 - Total[m]) Log[1 - p];

(* Find maximum likelihood estimates of a, b, and p *)
sol = NMinimize[{-2 loglikelihood + 2*3}, {a, b, logitp}, 
   WorkingPrecision -> 100, MaxIterations -> 50];
N[sol, 20]

(* Estimated variance/covariance matrix *)
plogL = D[loglikelihood, {{a, b, logitp}}];
plogL2 = D[plogL, {{a, b, logitp}}];
var = -Inverse[plogL2 /. sol[[2]]];

(* Standard errors of parameter estimates *)
sea = N[var[[1, 1]]^(1/2), 20]
seb = N[var[[2, 2]]^(1/2), 20]
sep = N[var[[3, 3]]^(1/2), 20]
